diagnoses.label: port-reuse leaves verifier port occupied
diagnoses.general_pattern: Skill guidance for self-verification of web outputs does not require the agent to release any background HTTP server (or use ephemeral ports) after validation, so a lingering server on a fixed port collides with the verifier that binds the same port and every browser-dependent test errors at fixture setup.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: Agent started a static server on port 8765 for a jsdom check; cleanup used `pkill -f "http.server 8765"` but the verifier's TCPServer bind on port 8765 subsequently failed with `OSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use`, causing 7 browser tests to ERROR at setup while file-existence tests passed.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Before finishing, verify that any agent-launched local server is fully stopped (process gone, port released) or was bound to an ephemeral port, and warn that reusing common serving ports may conflict with downstream verifiers.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Add explicit guidance in the D3 skill's interactive/verification section: prefer ephemeral ports (port 0) or short-lived subprocesses with explicit shutdown+wait, never leave background servers running, and document a teardown checklist (kill PID, poll port until free) before declaring the task complete.
diagnoses.target_section: Interactive features (tooltips, click handlers, hover effects) / self-verification of HTML outputs

diagnoses.label: no guidance on serving HTML outputs for verification
diagnoses.general_pattern: The skill tells the agent to produce standalone HTML using D3 but does not describe how to self-check outputs that rely on `d3.csv`/fetch (which fail under `file://`), leading the agent to improvise ad-hoc jsdom+HTTP-server setups whose side effects (installed packages, background processes, occupied ports) leak into the verifier environment.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: Agent installed jsdom into /tmp, spawned a python http.server, patched fetch polyfills, and iterated through multiple failing attempts (ESM require error, IPv6 ECONNREFUSED, missing fetch) before succeeding; the leftover server then broke the verifier.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Provide a lightweight, side-effect-free self-check recipe (or explicitly instruct the agent to skip runtime validation when the HTML uses fetch-based data loading) so the agent does not introduce environment state that outlives the task.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Document an approved verification pattern in the skill: e.g., static structural checks on generated HTML/JS, or a scoped headless-browser routine that uses ephemeral ports, context managers, and guaranteed teardown; explicitly forbid leaving servers or installed packages behind.
diagnoses.target_section: Outputs you should produce / Determinism rules (add a Verification subsection)

package_assessment.rationale: The generated artifacts passed all static file-existence and data-integrity tests; the browser-based tests failed solely because the agent left a background HTTP server bound to a fixed port (8765), which the verifier then could not bind. The skill lacks any guidance on safe self-verification of HTML outputs or teardown of agent-launched services, and adding such guidance would prevent the observed port-conflict failure without dictating task-specific answers.
